work: testimonia: Aristotle Metaphysics A.4; On Generation and Corruption I.8
locator: Aristotle Metaph. A.4 985b4-20 (DK 67 A6); GC I.8 325a23-b5 (DK 67 A7)
idea_year_note: c.; Leucippus and Democritus active c. 440-400 BCE; no dated text survives
claim: Everything is made of solid bodies too small to see, moving in empty space; things differ by the bodies' shape, order and position.
later_result: Atoms and molecules are physically real, countable bodies in thermal motion
confirm_event: Perrin, 'Mouvement brownien et realite moleculaire', Annales de chimie et de physique 8e ser. 18 (1909): concordant Avogadro numbers from independent Brownian measurements
causal_source: SEP 'Atomism from the 17th to the 20th Century' (17th-c. mechanical atomism as a revival of Greek atomism); no citation of the ancients by Dalton or Perrin found
same_passage_wrong: atoms uncuttable and partless; infinitely many atoms and shapes; one kind of matter differing only in shape (Dalton broke with this); qualities from atom shapes
instrument: compound microscope (water-immersion objective, camera lucida) on centrifuge-prepared gamboge/mastic emulsions

work: testimonia: Aristotle On Generation and Corruption I.8
locator: Aristotle GC I.8 325a23-b5 (DK 67 A7); SEP Democritus sec. 2
claim: The basic bodies cannot be cut or divided: each is a solid with no void inside it and no parts.
later_result: Atoms have separable parts (electrons; later the nucleus)
confirm_event: J.J. Thomson, 'Cathode Rays', Philosophical Magazine 5th ser. 44 (1897) 293-316: corpuscles about 1/1000 the mass of hydrogen, same from every gas and electrode
causal_source: the word 'atom' reached Thomson through Dalton's chemistry (1808); Thomson does not argue against Democritus
instrument: high-vacuum cathode-ray tube with electric and magnetic deflection

locator: Aët. 3.1.6 = DK 68 A91; Aristotle Meteor. I.8 345a25-31 = DK 59 A80
claim: The Milky Way is the combined glow of many small stars packed so closely that their light merges (Aëtius); Aristotle adds an Earth-shadow mechanism.
later_result: The Milky Way resolves into innumerable faint stars
confirm_event: Galileo, Sidereus Nuncius (Venice, March 1610): telescope resolves the Milky Way into a mass of innumerable stars
causal_source: Sidereus Nuncius names no ancient source for the finding (Carlos 1880 trans., Gutenberg 46036)
same_passage_wrong: in Aristotle's report the band is lit because Earth's shadow shields those stars from the Sun; Aristotle's rebuttals (band fixed among the stars; shadow cone too short) are correct

work: Letter to Herodotus (Diogenes Laertius 10); De Rerum Natura 2
idea_year_note: c.; Letter undated (Epicurus 341-270 BCE); Lucretius' clearer version c. 55 BCE
claim: Bodies fall at different speeds in water and air only because the medium resists; in empty space heavy and light bodies move equally fast.
later_result: In a vacuum all bodies fall with the same acceleration regardless of weight
confirm_event: Desaguliers, Phil. Trans. 30 (1717): guinea, paper and down-feather dropped together in an exhausted 8-ft compound receiver reach the bottom at the same instant
causal_source: Desaguliers frames the drop as proof of an 'interspersed vacuum' against plenists but names no ancient; no Galileo-Lucretius link found
same_passage_wrong: atoms move at one constant speed 'as quick as thought', with no acceleration; an absolute 'down' in infinite void; a swerve (clinamen) invented so atoms can collide
instrument: air pump with tall glass receiver

work: reported by Aristotle, De Anima II.7 and De Sensu 6
locator: Aristotle De An. II.7 418b20-26; De Sensu 6 446a24-b2
claim: Light moves through space: sunlight reaches the region between Sun and Earth before it reaches us, too fast for us to notice.
confirm_event: Romer, 'Demonstration touchant le mouvement de la lumiere', Journal des Scavans, 7 Dec 1676: Io eclipse timings show light takes about 22 min to cross Earth's orbit
causal_source: Romer 1676/1677 names no ancient author; the idea survived through Aristotle's refutation
same_passage_wrong: light as a material effluence; elsewhere vision by fire going out from the eye (DK 31 B84)
instrument: telescope plus pendulum clock timing of Io's eclipses

work: reported by Hippolytus, Refutatio 1.8; Plato Cratylus 409a
locator: Hippolytus Ref. 1.8.8-10 = DK 59 A42; Plato Crat. 409a
idea_year_note: c.; active at Athens c. 460-430 BCE
claim: The Moon has no light of its own but gets it from the Sun; the Moon is eclipsed when Earth comes between, the Sun when the Moon does.
later_result: Moonlight is reflected sunlight; eclipses are shadow geometry
confirm_event: Aristarchus, On the Sizes and Distances of the Sun and Moon (c. 270 BCE): hypothesis 1, Moon receives its light from the Sun, used to measure the Sun's distance
causal_source: Plato, Cratylus 409a, calls it Anaxagoras' recent claim; Heath 1913 ch. X collects the transmission (Plutarch, Aetius); Aristarchus himself names no source
same_passage_wrong: some lunar eclipses caused by invisible bodies below the Moon; Sun a fiery stone bigger than the Peloponnese only; flat Earth riding on air
instrument: naked-eye angle measurement (half-Moon elongation, eclipse shadow width)

work: reported by Hippolytus Ref. 1.6; Aristotle De Caelo II.13
locator: Hippolytus Ref. 1.6.3 (DK 12 A11); Aristotle De Caelo II.13 295b10-16 (DK 12 A26)
claim: The Earth hangs aloft, held up by nothing; it stays put because it is equally far from everything, so has no reason to move any one way.
later_result: Earth is an unsupported body held in orbit by gravitation
confirm_event: Newton, Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica (London, 1687), Book III
causal_source: no line to Newton; Aristotle transmits and rejects the argument (De Caelo II.13)
same_passage_wrong: Earth is a stone drum at rest at the centre; reason is symmetry, not force; stars nearer than Moon and Sun; heavenly bodies are fire rings seen through vents
instrument: Tycho Brahe's naked-eye positional data (via Kepler's laws) plus telescopic satellite periods

work: Diogenes Laertius 8.85; Aristotle De Caelo II.13; Aëtius 3.13
locator: D.L. 8.85 (DK 44 A1); Aristotle De Caelo II.13 293a18-27; Aët. 3.13.1-2 (DK 44 A21, number unverified)
idea_year_note: c.; Philolaus c. 470-385 BCE, book late 5th c. BCE
claim: Earth is not at the centre but is one of the stars, carried round a central fire, and its motion produces night and day.
confirm_event: Bradley, 'A new discovered motion of the fix'd stars' (aberration of light), Philosophical Transactions 35 (1729) 637-661
causal_source: Copernicus, De Revolutionibus (1543), dedication to Paul III, quotes Plutarch (Placita 3.13) that Philolaus moved the Earth round the fire in an oblique circle
same_passage_wrong: central fire and counter-earth (do not exist); a daily circuit rather than an annual orbit; the Sun a glassy body reflecting fire; motive numerological
instrument: zenith sector (Graham; Molyneux's 24.5 ft at Kew 1725, Bradley's 12.5 ft at Wanstead 1727)

work: Letter to Herodotus; De Rerum Natura 1
idea_year_note: c.; Letter undated; Lucretius c. 55 BCE
claim: Nothing comes into being from nothing and nothing is destroyed into nothing; the sum of things always was and always will be as it is now.
later_result: Conservation of mass in chemical change
confirm_event: Lavoisier, Traite elementaire de chimie (Paris, 1789), Part I ch. XIII: nothing is created; equal matter before and after every operation
causal_source: Lavoisier states it as an 'axiom' and cites no ancient (Kerr trans., Gutenberg 30775)
same_passage_wrong: what is conserved is the uncuttable atoms (atoms transmute; rest mass alone is not conserved); the universe unchanging as a whole

claim: Specks tumbling in a sunbeam are knocked about by unseen blows; motion climbs from atoms to small clusters to visible specks, a picture of atoms' endless motion.
later_result: Brownian motion is caused by molecular impacts
confirm_event: Perrin, Comptes rendus 146 (1908) 967-970: height distribution of Brownian grains confirms the molecular-kinetic theory
causal_source: Perrin (Soddy trans. 1910) explicitly sets aside the dust-in-sunlight comparison and names no ancient
same_passage_wrong: visible motes are moved mainly by air currents, not molecular impacts (Perrin's own objection); atoms move at constant speed downward through void
instrument: compound microscope on centrifuge-prepared gamboge emulsions
